title: How to identify DSO-affiliated dental practices
summary: Check dental group affiliation and route software prospects to the right buying team.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


Research dental support organization affiliation before assigning a practice to an independent-only SaaS segment. Use explicit practice disclosures and group announcements, keep dated evidence, and confirm purchasing responsibility for the workflow you sell.


- A practice name is a discovery clue; affiliation needs a source.
- Support arrangements can differ from clinical decision-making.
- An unresolved relationship should remain visible in your sales research.


Dental software sellers need to know both the practice they are researching and the organization that can evaluate the product. Scheduling, patient communications, billing, and clinical workflows may involve different teams. This guide focuses on affiliation research; use[the dental SaaS prospecting guide](https://www.openmart.com/blogs/find-independent-dental-practices-software-sales) to build the broader account list.


## 1. Define the relationship you need to establish


Create separate fields for the practice brand, practice domain, disclosed support organization, and confirmed software evaluator. Do not collapse these into a single “owner” field. A DSO relationship can support routing decisions while leaving the purchasing process unresolved.


Choose the segment before researching. An independent-only pilot should keep affiliated and unresolved practices outside its confirmed account count. A group-focused sales motion can keep those records and research the relevant group team. Neither segment is inherently better; the product and sales process determine fit.


## 2. Start with the practice profile and its own website


Use[Openmart’s dental practice database](https://www.openmart.com/databases/dentists) for initial business discovery. Review the practice’s website for team information, support disclosures, location pages, and links to a parent or support organization. Save the domain and source URL with the date checked. Read the page itself rather than inferring affiliation from a search-result title.


A dentist’s biography confirms what it says about that person. It does not automatically establish ownership of the practice entity or authority to purchase software. Ask about the relevant workflow when those responsibilities are unclear.


## 3. Cross-check group announcements


Search the named group’s own website for affiliation announcements or supported-office information. Heartland Dental’s[May 2026 update](https://blog.heartland.com/heartland-dental-monthly-growth-spotlight-may-2026) names several affiliated offices under local practice names. That is concrete evidence to attach to a relationship field, rather than a reason to assume all similarly named practices belong to the same group.


An announcement is dated evidence. If it conflicts with a newer disclosure, keep both URLs and resolve the discrepancy. When neither source establishes the relationship, mark it unresolved and leave it out of the confirmed independent count.


## 4. Keep affiliation separate from the buying decision


Heartland’s[description of its support model](https://heartland.com/how-it-works/) includes administrative support such as scheduling and patient communications. That context helps a software seller prepare a routing question. It does not identify the evaluator for a specific product or prove a practice’s current technology stack.


Ask a focused question: “Who evaluates changes to patient communication software for this office: the practice team or a shared operations team?” Record the answer and its scope. A confirmed evaluator for one workflow may not be the evaluator for every software category.


## 5. Build an auditable affiliation worksheet


- Practice brand and domain: the business being researched.
- Relationship status: disclosed affiliation, confirmed independent, or unresolved.
- Organization name: enter only when supported by evidence.
- Evidence URL and date: preserve both the publication date and review date.
- Workflow: the software category you are qualifying.
- Evaluator: confirmed role, team, or unresolved.
- Next action: group routing, independent account research, or follow-up verification.


These are research-sheet fields, not a promise that every field is populated in a database. Keep missing evidence visible. For a 25-account pilot, report the number with a verified relationship and the number still unresolved. Do not replace unresolved records with assumed independence to improve the apparent match rate.


## Recommendation


Start with[dental practice discovery](https://www.openmart.com/databases/dentists) , then attach first-party affiliation evidence to each account. Choose whether the account belongs in the independent or group sales motion before discussing product fit.[Start your dental account research in Openmart](https://app.openmart.com/register?utm_source=openmart_blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=tam_pilot&utm_content=identify-dso-affiliated-dental-practices) .


## FAQs


**Does a DSO affiliation establish the software buyer?**


It establishes a relationship when supported by evidence. Confirm who evaluates the particular workflow before choosing the sales route.


**Can a local practice name prove independence?**


No. Affiliated practices can retain local names. Check explicit disclosures and organization announcements.


**What should I do when sources disagree?**


Keep both source URLs and their dates, flag the account, and resolve the relationship before counting it as confirmed.


*Research method reviewed October 2, 2026. Public examples illustrate verification decisions and are not customer results or current data exports.*
